limits.notes: Primary lime source for calcium silicates; adequate CaO supports alite (C3S) and early Type I strength, while excess raises free-lime risk and unsoundness.
Forms C3S and C2S with lime; sufficient SiO2 builds silicate strength potential, while excess raises the silica ratio and makes the mix harder to burn.
Forms C3A and kiln liquid phase; higher Al2O3 increases heat of hydration and speeds set but weakens sulfate resistance.
Forms C4AF and provides clinkering flux; higher Fe2O3 darkens OPC and fluidizes melt, while low Fe2O3 reduces burnability and shifts balance toward C3A.
Excess magnesia (periclase) can cause delayed expansion and unsoundness in hardened concrete; ASTM C150 Type I limits MgO to ≤ 6.0%.
Regulates set with C3A via gypsum; excess SO3 risks false set and sulfate-related expansion, so ASTM C150 caps SO3 at 3.0% (C3A ≤ 8%) or 3.5% (C3A > 8%).
High loss on ignition indicates prehydration, carbonation, or incomplete calcination and can reduce strength consistency; ASTM C150 Type I allows ≤ 3.0% (≤ 3.5% if limestone is an ingredient).
Insoluble residue marks non-reactive contamination or underburned material that dilutes reactive clinker phases; ASTM C150 Type I limits IR to ≤ 1.5%.
Uncombined CaO causes delayed expansion and unsoundness in hardened paste; elevated free lime also signals incomplete burning or over-limed feed.
Lime saturation index controlling alite potential: higher LSF favors C3S and early strength but raises free-lime risk; lower LSF favors belite and weaker early strength.

Silica modulus (SiO2/(Al2O3+Fe2O3)): higher SR increases silicate content but reduces liquid phase and burnability; lower SR increases melt and can soften clinker with lower silicate strength potential.

Alumina modulus (Al2O3/Fe2O3) balances C3A vs C4AF: higher AR raises heat of hydration and weakens sulfate resistance; lower AR darkens cement and slows early strength while improving sulfate resistance.
Checks analytical integrity of the oxide report; sums outside ~95–105% make LSF, SR, AR, and Bogue phases unreliable for Type I quality decisions.
Alite is the main early-strength phase in Type I OPC; higher C3S accelerates hydration and early compressive strength through about 28 days.
Belite hydrates slowly and supports later-age strength; excess C2S (low C3S) weakens early Type I strength, while very low C2S often signals an over-limed mix.
Tricalcium aluminate drives early heat and setting; high C3A reduces sulfate resistance and raises the ASTM SO3 ceiling when C3A exceeds 8%.
Ferrite acts as clinkering flux with little strength contribution; higher C4AF darkens OPC and aids sulfate resistance, while low C4AF reduces melt and can raise C3A if alumina stays high.
